title: Shivam Pandit Is Two Days Away: The 'Awarapan 2' Teaser Drops on the Original's 19th Anniversary
excerpt: Emraan Hashmi, Disha Patani, and Shabana Azmi's first-ever villain role — a cult classic gets its sequel, its reimagined music, and a month-long blitz before its Independence Day clash with Sunny Deol.
body:
The announcement came not from a press conference or a media house, but from **Sony Music India's** Twitter account at dusk on Friday: a moody poster, a few lines of verse, and a date. *"Unveiling the Soul of Awarapan 2 — A Melody, A Memory, A New Journey Begins. Teaser out on June 29th."* And just like that, nineteen years after a brooding, tragic love story quietly became one of Bollywood's most enduring cult films, **Shivam Pandit** is walking back into the light.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=K3luM8xdtyg</youtube>

The teaser of **Awarapan 2** arrives this Sunday — and the date is not an accident. June 29, 2026, marks exactly nineteen years since the original *Awarapan* opened in theatres in 2007. Back then, **Emraan Hashmi** played Shivam with a stillness that felt dangerous, a man caught between duty and devotion, and the film sank at the box office before rising, year after year, into something the industry rarely produces: a genuine cult. The songs — Pritam's aching *Toh Phir Aao*, Sayeed Quadri's devastating *Tera Mera Rishta* — became the unofficial soundtrack of an entire generation's heartbreak playlists. Producer **Vishesh Bhatt** has chosen to honour all of that by turning the teaser launch into an anniversary tribute.

## The Story Picks Up Where the Dream Ended

The original *Awarapan* closed on one of Hindi cinema's most haunting final shots: Shivam, bleeding out, hallucinating a reunion with Shriya Saran's Aaliya in a dream sequence that felt too beautiful to be real. And that, it turns out, is exactly where the sequel begins. According to earlier reports in Mid-Day, **Awarapan 2 is a continuation, not a reboot** — Shivam comes back to life and crosses paths with a new woman, played by **Disha Patani**, who becomes essential to his next mission.

Disha, who shot extensively in Bangkok alongside Emraan during a 40-day schedule in late 2025, is an interesting choice. The makers clearly wanted someone who could hold a frame with physical command and minimal dialogue — the same quality Shriya brought to the first film. Whether the chemistry translates is something the teaser will need to answer, and fast.

And then there is **Shabana Azmi**, who has never — in five decades and over 100 films — played a villain. Until now. The veteran actress steps into what is reportedly a cold, manipulative antagonist role, the kind of casting that makes you sit up and lean forward. Director **Nitin Kakkar** (of *Filmistaan* fame) is steering this sequel, having taken over from original director Mohit Suri, and the decision to anchor the film's tension around an actress of Azmi's calibre tells you something about the ambition.

## The Music Is Coming Back — and It's Personal

If the story of Awarapan was always about longing, the music was the evidence. And the makers know it. According to Pinkvilla's exclusive report, the sequel's soundtrack will include **reimagined versions of both *Toh Phir Aao* and *Tera Mera Rishta***, with **Mithoon** and **Sayeed Quadri** returning to rework the tracks they helped make iconic. These won't be lazy remixes dropped into a trailer for nostalgia points — the team has reportedly treated the music album as the film's single biggest asset, with newly composed melodies sitting alongside the legacy tracks.

> "The makers have planned a month-long promotional strategy of Awarapan 2, ensuring to take the hype and buzz around the film a notch higher." — Pinkvilla source

The promotional rollout starts imminently: a digital logo reveal from Vishesh Bhatt, then the teaser, then the music launch. For a film that was never meant to be a franchise — *Awarapan* was, after all, a modest mid-budget drama — the scale of the campaign signals real confidence.

## August 14 — and a Patriotic Collision

**Awarapan 2** is locked for an **August 14, 2026** release — the Independence Day weekend, Bollywood's most lucrative summer slot. But it will not have the runway to itself. **Sunny Deol's *Lahore 1947***, a partition-era drama directed by Rajkumar Santoshi and produced by Aamir Khan, arrives on August 13, just one day earlier. Two very different films — one a brooding, music-drenched action romance, the other a patriotic period piece — fighting for the same screens, the same weekend, the same national mood.

For Emraan, the timing is strategic. After *Murder 3* in 2013, the actor's box-office trajectory cooled. But between Awarapan 2 and his upcoming musical horror **Rooh** (which begins shooting in October with two leading ladies and director Mayank Sharma), he is building a late-career surge that leans into exactly what made him a star in the first place: intensity, edge, and songs you cannot shake.

## Where to Watch

**Awarapan 2** hits theatres worldwide on **August 14, 2026**. The teaser drops **this Sunday, June 29** — mark your calendars, cue up *Toh Phir Aao*, and prepare to feel something. Shivam Pandit is almost here.

*For diaspora audiences in the US, UK, and Canada, theatrical screenings are expected across major chains. Details on international distribution will follow the teaser launch.*
